AFPDF-01.text: TIMING used a 3 percentage-point noninferiority margin. Early treatment was within 4 days; randomization occurred within 72 hours. The indexed TIMING correction body remains unavailable; this repair is limited to the paired original report.
AFPDF-01.title: TIMING: noninferiority margin

AFPDF-02.text: ELAN used an estimation design without a prespecified superiority or noninferiority hypothesis. Early DOAC: within 48 hours for minor/moderate stroke, days 6-7 for major stroke. Later: days 3-4 for minor, 6-7 for moderate, 12-14 for major. Overall admission NIHSS was median 5 (IQR 2-11); the randomization NIHSS median was 3. A universal enrollment cutoff of 100 hours is not established by the cited main report. The recovered PDF declares an update on June 29, 2023; the update substance was not independently reconciled.
AFPDF-02.title: ELAN: study design and treatment windows

AFPDF-03.text: START allowed selected hemorrhagic transformation at investigator discretion. Exclusions included infarct volume greater than half the MCA territory, or NIHSS greater than 23 if the lesion extent was not visible. For days 3-4, 6, 10 and 14, ischemic events were 0/3/2/2 and hemorrhagic events 1/1/1/0: the composite counts were 1/4/3/2. Randomized arm sizes were 54/53/46/47. The trial did not identify a clearly superior start day.
AFPDF-03.title: START: eligibility and composite events

AFPDF-04.text: Hemorrhagic transformation is heterogeneous. The ELAN analysis included centrally identified PH2 despite protocol exclusions and reported possible worse functional outcome with early treatment in patients with parenchymal hemorrhage. Nonsignificant interaction tests do not establish subgroup safety. The ELAN HT erratum (PMID 38950115) was identified but its body remains unread; the repair therefore withholds blanket reassurance rather than declaring corrected-current subgroup clearance.
AFPDF-04.title: Hemorrhagic transformation: limits of reassurance

AFPDF-05.text: CATALYST reported mean age 77.7 years (SD 10.0), not median age. The pooled sample comprised 5,441 participants.
AFPDF-05.title: CATALYST: mean age

AFPDF-06.text: Eligibility must be interpreted separately for each trial. A universal exclusion list using infarct greater than two-thirds MCA territory, blood pressure 185/110, or all PH2 is not established across these trials. OPTIMAS excluded PH2 and a decision already made for surgery requiring anticoagulant interruption or delay during the first week; the protocol encouraged approach within 72 hours, but the early strategy allowed treatment within 96 hours. These trial windows do not constitute a universal bedside algorithm.
AFPDF-06.title: Trial-specific eligibility and timing

AFPDF-07.text: The randomized comparison was an early versus delayed DOAC strategy. Antiplatelet use during the delay is a co-intervention, not automatically a failure of randomization. Its direction of effect on a composite containing ischemia and bleeding was not established by the cited trials; a claim of bias toward the null has been removed.
AFPDF-07.title: Antiplatelet co-interventions and causal interpretation

AFPDF-08.text: In CATALYST, the roughly 30% relative reduction describes the primary 30-day composite. Recurrent ischemic stroke had an odds ratio of 0.66, with an approximately 34% crude relative risk reduction. The pooled finding is not proof of safety in every hemorrhagic-transformation phenotype.
AFPDF-08.title: CATALYST: composite versus ischemic-stroke effect

AFPDF-09.text: The retained cells reproduce 2023 AF guideline Table 19, but must be read with its footnotes. Apixaban 2.5 mg twice daily applies when at least two of these are present: age at least 80 years, weight at most 60 kg, serum creatinine at least 1.5 mg/dL. ARISTOTLE excluded creatinine greater than 2.5 mg/dL or calculated CrCl less than 25 mL/min. Nonrenal considerations, including interactions, also apply. Gray cells identify doses not studied in pivotal trials. For rivaroxaban at CrCl less than 15, the guideline notes limited pharmacokinetic data and distinguishes the AF indication from other indications. This archived guideline table is not a stand-alone dosing instruction: current drug labeling and individual eligibility must be checked. The three indexed AF2023 correction bodies were reviewed separately; none changed these numbered recommendations or Table 19. The cropped slide does not reliably preserve evidence shading: consult the full source Table 19 rather than interpreting this image's gray rows as evidence categories.
AFPDF-09.title: Renal DOAC table: essential footnotes

AFPDF-10.text: TIMING randomized patients within 72 hours, comparing DOAC initiation within 4 days with initiation on days 5-10. Noninferiority was demonstrated using a 3 percentage-point margin; superiority was not demonstrated. Do not substitute the randomization window for the treatment window.
AFPDF-10.title: TIMING: randomization versus treatment window

AFPDF-11.text: Keep endpoints and analysis populations separate. AVERROES: stroke/systemic embolism was 3.7%/year with aspirin and 1.6%/year with apixaban; major bleeding was 1.2%/year and 1.4%/year, respectively. ARTESIA: primary stroke/systemic embolism was 1.24%/patient-year with aspirin and 0.78%/patient-year with apixaban (intention-to-treat); major bleeding was 0.94% and 1.71%/patient-year (on-treatment). The 1.02%/0.64% pair in ARTESIA was ischemic or unknown stroke, not its primary endpoint. The original table combined different populations/endpoints and time-unspecified NNT/NNH; it has been replaced without cross-trial efficacy ranking.
AFPDF-11.title: Cross-trial comparison: endpoints and analysis populations

AFPDF-12.text: After TAVI with AF, ENVISAGE met noninferiority for its composite endpoint, but major bleeding was higher with edoxaban: 9.7 versus 7.0 events per 100 patient-years; HR 1.40 (95% CI 1.03-1.91). ATLANTIS did not demonstrate apixaban superiority; its anticoagulation-indicated stratum was exploratory, not an equivalence demonstration. The ATLANTIS erratum body remains unread, so correction-current clearance is not claimed.
AFPDF-12.title: TAVI with AF: trial-specific benefit and bleeding

AFPDF-13.text: The AF2023 warfarin exception specifies rheumatic mitral stenosis or mitral stenosis of moderate or greater severity, and mechanical valves. It does not apply to all rheumatic valve disease or all degrees of nonrheumatic mitral stenosis. Source: section 6.8.5, recommendations for AF in valvular heart disease.
AFPDF-13.title: Valve disease: warfarin exception scope

AFPDF-14.text: The AZALEA secondary analysis Table 1 reports prior ischemic stroke in 191 of 1,287 participants (14.9%). A blanket prior-stroke exclusion is incorrect. This repair does not update all trial recruitment statuses elsewhere on the archived slide.
AFPDF-14.title: AZALEA: participants with prior stroke

AFPDF-15.text: CHA2DS2-VASc hypertension includes current antihypertensive treatment, including controlled treated hypertension; it is not limited to a currently elevated blood pressure. Source: AF2023 Table 10 risk-factor definition. Original absolute-risk bar values were not traced to a primary cohort; they have been withheld as individual risk estimates. Absolute risk varies with population, endpoint, follow-up and competing risks.
AFPDF-15.title: Stroke-risk scores: hypertension and calibration

AFPDF-16.text: RATE found that brief device-detected episodes were not associated with clinical events. A bare 20-second label is not a validated stroke-risk or anticoagulation threshold. The exact recording-duration definition was not verified from the full paper; this repair is limited to the primary abstract conclusion.
AFPDF-16.title: RATE: brief episodes are not a treatment threshold

AFPDF-17.text: Historical WATCHMAN FLX labeling specifies anticoagulant plus aspirin initially; after approximately 45-day TEE, anticoagulant cessation is conditional on device seal and thrombus assessment. Aspirin plus a P2Y12 inhibitor then continues until six months after implantation, followed by aspirin. Six months is measured from implantation, not from the 45-day visit. This restores the historical sequence, not a current universal device regimen; current device-specific instructions and alternatives were not reviewed. Sources: FDA P130013S035C, physical pages 59-60, and PINNACLE FLX methods.
AFPDF-17.title: WATCHMAN: historical antithrombotic sequence

AFPDF-18.text: RESTART enrolled selected survivors of ICH that occurred while using antithrombotics, randomized a median 76 days after ICH. Its results do not establish antiplatelet safety for every ICH phenotype or start time, and aspirin is not a substitute for AF anticoagulation. A universal aspirin-safety statement has been replaced with this population and timing qualification.
AFPDF-18.title: RESTART: population and timing limits

AFPDF-19.text: The teal bars reproduce FinACAF CHA2DS2-VA estimates for the 2017-2018 stratum; the blue comparator is Friberg CHA2DS2-VASc. These are different score definitions and cohorts, with different methods and competing risks. Publication years (2024 and 2012) are not enrollment years. The contrast cannot be attributed to time alone. The teaching question now asks how these design differences limit comparison; proposed causal explanations are not established findings.
AFPDF-19.title: Risk-score comparisons: cohort and method differences

AFPDF-20.text: The figure and associated pooled analysis are CATALYST, an individual participant data meta-analysis of 5,441 participants. The hidden ELAN Trial (n=2,013) heading and overlaid text have been removed from the PDF content, not simply covered.
AFPDF-20.title: CATALYST: pooled sample identity

AFPDF-21.text: ELAN Table 2 reports mRS 0-2 in 62.6%/62.6% at 30 days and 66.6%/65.8% at 90 days (early/later). OPTIMAS main report explicitly deferred functional outcomes to another publication; its recovered main report and supplement did not support the previously shown functional percentages or ordinal odds ratio. For archival provenance only, the unverified OPTIMAS values were 52.8%/52.5%, ordinal OR 1.00 (0.90-1.12), p=0.96. They are not validated results; their source remains unresolved. OPTIMAS PDF declares a January 2, 2025 correction; the whole notice remains unread.
AFPDF-21.title: Functional outcomes: timepoints and source gaps

AFPDF-22.text: CATALYST used a one-stage generalized linear mixed-effects model with a trial random effect; its primary odds ratios were unadjusted for patient-level covariates. Trial-specific endpoint ascertainment was retained, rather than new central blinded readjudication of all outcomes. Supplement Table S1 reports no event adjudication for TIMING and differing endpoint definitions.
AFPDF-22.title: CATALYST: statistical model and adjudication

AFPDF-23.text: CATALYST Figure 3 reports NIHSS interaction p=0.54 across four strata, not a dedicated safety test for NIHSS at least 11. The cited main report and supplement did not report an HT interaction p=0.61; HT analysis was described as future work. No absence-of-harm inference should be made from a nonsignificant interaction. ELAN HT evidence has separate limitations in Repair 04.
AFPDF-23.title: CATALYST: subgroup interaction limits

AFPDF-24.text: CATALYST supplement Figure S2 gives a common-effect OR 0.713 (95% CI 0.505-1.005) and random-effects OR 0.721 (0.510-1.020). Both confidence intervals include 1. The previously asserted significant aggregate sensitivity result has been corrected. Exact per-protocol and leave-one-out estimates on the original slide were not located in the recovered main report/supplement; they remain unverified, not proven false. Archival provenance only: per-protocol n=5,110, OR 0.69 (0.49-0.98), p=0.037; leave-one-out ORs without TIMING 0.69 (0.48-0.99), without ELAN 0.83 (0.54-1.28), without OPTIMAS 0.61 (0.39-0.97), without START 0.70 (0.49-0.99). These exact figures are not validated by the sources acquired.
AFPDF-24.title: CATALYST: sensitivity analyses and source gaps

AFPDF-25.text: OPTIMAS supplement Table e1 reports 816 reduced-dose recipients: 378 apixaban, 21 dabigatran, 369 edoxaban, 48 rivaroxaban. Of these, 155 (19.0%) were classified as underdosed using NICE guidance (88/4/52/11). Reduced dosing was therefore not uniformly guideline-concordant. The originally displayed drug-choice interaction p=0.37 was not located in the recovered sources and is not treated as validated.
AFPDF-25.title: OPTIMAS: reduced dosing and concordance

findings.explanation: TIMING specified a 3% noninferiority margin. The timing deck reports 2.5%; the July 2024 deck p19 correctly reports 3%.
findings.recommended_disposition: Consolidated review recommendation only; no source or PDF modification made. Correct or explicitly annotate the affected archived slide before reuse as current teaching.

findings.title: ELAN design and moderate later-arm timing misrepresented
findings.explanation: ELAN used an estimation design without a prespecified superiority or noninferiority hypothesis. Its later moderate-stroke group started on days 6–7, not days 3–4. Recovered main paper also fails to establish a universal<100h population,and shows overall admission NIHSS5(IQR2–11),not unqualified2–12 on PDF02p17.
findings.recommended_disposition: Consolidated review recommendation only; no source or PDF modification made. Correct or explicitly annotate the affected archived slide before reuse as current teaching.

findings.title: START eligibility and primary outcome table are wrong
findings.explanation: START allowed selected hemorrhagic transformation. NIHSS >23 exclusion was conditional on lesion visibility. The displayed 1/3/2/2 event counts mix the early-arm hemorrhagic count with later ischemic counts; composite counts were 1/4/3/2.
findings.recommended_disposition: Consolidated review recommendation only; no source or PDF modification made. Correct or explicitly annotate the affected archived slide before reuse as current teaching.

findings.title: Blanket hemorrhagic-transformation reassurance suppresses an important PH limitation
findings.explanation: Blanket reassurance for hemorrhagic transformation is too strong. The ELAN HT analysis includes centrally identified PH2 and reports possible worse functional outcome with early treatment in PH. START allowed selected HT. A nonsignificant interaction does not establish subgroup safety. ELAN HT correction body remains unavailable.
findings.recommended_disposition: Consolidated review recommendation only; no source or PDF modification made. Correct or explicitly annotate the affected archived slide before reuse as current teaching.

findings.title: CATALYST mean age labeled median
findings.explanation: CATALYST reports mean age 77.7 years (SD 10.0), not median age.
findings.recommended_disposition: Consolidated review recommendation only; no source or PDF modification made. Correct or explicitly annotate the affected archived slide before reuse as current teaching.

findings.title: Universal timing-trial exclusion list not established
findings.explanation: The slides present a common fixed exclusion list that is not supported across trials. Recovered OPTIMAS protocol confirms a pre-randomization decision for surgery requiring interruption/delay of anticoagulation within week1 as an exclusion; that component is no longer unresolved. It does not impose a fixed>2/3-MCA cutoff. Ideally approaching patients within72h is not a hard eligibility limit. General clinician contraindications must not be replaced with invented universal thresholds.
findings.recommended_disposition: Consolidated review recommendation only; no source or PDF modification made. Correct or explicitly annotate the affected archived slide before reuse as current teaching.

findings.title: Antiplatelet bridging described as established confounding toward the null
findings.explanation: Antiplatelet use within a randomized early-versus-delayed strategy does not automatically invalidate randomization. Direction of its effect on an ischemic-plus-bleeding composite is not established. The slides present an unverified causal interpretation as a methodological fact.
findings.recommended_disposition: Consolidated review recommendation only; no source or PDF modification made. Correct or explicitly annotate the affected archived slide before reuse as current teaching.

findings.title: CATALYST ischemic-stroke relative reduction confused with composite
findings.explanation: Approximately 30% relative reduction describes the CATALYST primary composite. The crude ischemic-stroke reduction is approximately 34%, with OR 0.66.
findings.recommended_disposition: Consolidated review recommendation only; no source or PDF modification made. Correct or explicitly annotate the affected archived slide before reuse as current teaching.

findings.title: Renal DOAC table omits essential dosing and evidence footnotes
findings.explanation: AF2023 Table 19 footnotes specify the apixaban reduction criteria (at least two of age ≥80, weight ≤60 kg, serum creatinine ≥1.5 mg/dL), pivotal renal exclusions, nonrenal considerations and limited evidence for some doses. The slide crops these footnotes while retaining their symbols.
findings.recommended_disposition: Consolidated review recommendation only; no source or PDF modification made. Correct or explicitly annotate the affected archived slide before reuse as current teaching.

findings.title: TIMING early-treatment window confused with randomization window
findings.explanation: TIMING randomized within 72 hours of stroke onset, but the early treatment window was ≤4 days. These are different time limits.
findings.recommended_disposition: Consolidated review recommendation only; no source or PDF modification made. Correct or explicitly annotate the affected archived slide before reuse as current teaching.

findings.title: Cross-trial counseling table mixes endpoints and misleading NNT/NNH
findings.explanation: AVERROES major bleeding was 1.2%/year with aspirin and 1.4% with apixaban, not 3.8%/4.5%. ARTESIA primary stroke/systemic-embolism rates were 1.24%/0.78%, not 1.02%/0.64%. The derived NNH 143 and NNT 263 do not represent the declared endpoints. Recovered ARTESIA Table2 identifies the1.02%/.64% pair as ischemic-or-unknown stroke,confirming the endpoint substitution.
findings.recommended_disposition: Consolidated review recommendation only; no source or PDF modification made. Correct or explicitly annotate the affected archived slide before reuse as current teaching.

findings.title: Post-TAVI DOAC equivalence shorthand hides major bleeding and exploratory design
findings.explanation: ENVISAGE met composite noninferiority but edoxaban increased major bleeding: 9.7 versus 7.0 events per 100 patient-years, HR 1.40 (1.03–1.91). ATLANTIS did not establish apixaban superiority; its AF stratum comparison was exploratory, not an equivalence demonstration.
findings.recommended_disposition: Consolidated review recommendation only; no source or PDF modification made. Correct or explicitly annotate the affected archived slide before reuse as current teaching.

findings.title: Warfarin exception expanded to all rheumatic disease or all mitral stenosis
findings.explanation: AF2023 specifies rheumatic mitral stenosis or mitral stenosis of moderate or greater severity, and mechanical valves. Other valve disease is not a blanket warfarin-only exception.
findings.recommended_disposition: Consolidated review recommendation only; no source or PDF modification made. Correct or explicitly annotate the affected archived slide before reuse as current teaching.

findings.title: AZALEA incorrectly said to exclude prior stroke
findings.explanation: The primary AZALEA analysis Table 1 reports prior ischemic stroke in 191/1,287 participants (14.9%). A blanket exclusion of prior stroke is therefore false. Registry omissions alone would not have established this.
findings.recommended_disposition: Consolidated review recommendation only; no source or PDF modification made. Correct or explicitly annotate the affected archived slide before reuse as current teaching.

findings.title: Risk-score shorthand can miss treated hypertension and lacks cohort calibration
findings.explanation: CHA2DS2-VASc hypertension includes current antihypertensive treatment, not only currently elevated BP. A compact table should not omit controlled treated hypertension. The adjacent absolute-risk bars also require cohort context; their original values remain unverified.
findings.confidence: high for hypertension definition; unresolved for original rate bars
findings.recommended_disposition: Consolidated review recommendation only; no source or PDF modification made. Correct or explicitly annotate the affected archived slide before reuse as current teaching.

findings.title: RATE20-second entry can imply a validated risk threshold
findings.explanation: RATE concluded that brief device-detected episodes were not associated with clinical events. A bare 20-second bullet under burden and stroke risk can be misread as a validated risk or treatment threshold. The exact recording-duration definition was not verified from the full paper.
findings.recommended_disposition: Consolidated review recommendation only; no source or PDF modification made. Correct or explicitly annotate the affected archived slide before reuse as current teaching.

findings.title: WATCHMAN FLX postimplant sequence skips DAPT
findings.explanation: The historical WATCHMAN FLX label specifies aspirin plus a P2Y12 inhibitor after TEE-guided OAC cessation at about 45 days, continuing until six months after implantation, then aspirin. Page 43 skips this DAPT phase; page 41 should clarify that six months is measured from implantation. Current device-specific alternatives need current IFU review.
findings.recommended_disposition: Consolidated review recommendation only; no source or PDF modification made. Correct or explicitly annotate the affected archived slide before reuse as current teaching.

findings.title: Aspirin resumption called universally safe after ICH
findings.explanation: RESTART studied selected ICH survivors who had previously used antithrombotics, randomized a median 76 days after ICH. It does not establish safety for every ICH phenotype or start time, or support aspirin as a substitute for AF anticoagulation.
findings.recommended_disposition: Consolidated review recommendation only; no source or PDF modification made. Correct or explicitly annotate the affected archived slide before reuse as current teaching.

findings.title: Discussion compares different risk scores as a temporal trend
findings.explanation: FinACAF teal bars match CHA2DS2-VA in the 2017–2018 stratum. The comparator is presented as CHA2DS2-VASc. Different score definitions, countries, cohorts and competing-risk methods prevent attributing the contrast to time alone. Publication years are not observation years; proposed explanations remain hypotheses.
findings.recommended_disposition: Consolidated review recommendation only; no source or PDF modification made. Correct or explicitly annotate the affected archived slide before reuse as current teaching.

findings.title: Overlaid CATALYST/ELAN heading confuses pooled sample identity
